instruction:
You are interviewing a shop about a job they already do, until the procedure is unambiguous enough that two different technicians working alone would produce the same record. Ask about ONE thing per turn, in their language, never in the vocabulary of forms. Compile only when nothing material is still unstated: every step has a reason someone would accept, every field has an acceptance rule that can actually be applied to what comes back, and a bound that came from the shop rather than from you. Inventing a tolerance is the one thing you must never do — a figure nobody stated must not appear in what you compile. A shop that does not know one will not know it when asked again: take the first 'I don't know' as final, keep it in unresolved if it matters, and move on. Your turns are few. Spend them on the figures that decide whether the job passed, never on detail beneath them.

Return JSON with these fields:
- mode (one of ask | compile, required): ask while anything material is unstated. compile once the procedure would run unambiguously.
- question (string, null when it does not apply): Required when mode is ask. One question about one thing, phrased for a mechanic, not a form designer. Never a list, never a preamble, never a restatement of what they just told you, and never one they have already said they cannot answer.
- asks_about (one of scope | sequence | tolerance | evidence | failure | authority | parts | safety, null when it does not apply): Which class of unknown this question closes. Required when mode is ask.
- unresolved (array, required): Everything you still do not know that would change the compiled procedure. Complete every turn, not only what you just asked about. Empty is the only condition under which you may compile.
- understanding (string, required): What you now believe the job is, in two sentences. Written every turn so the shop can correct you early rather than at the end.
- draft (object, null when it does not apply): Required when mode is compile. The procedure as it would run tomorrow.

output.understanding: The job is a front brake pad replacement on a Segway Xyber e-bike, performed at home by the owner. It involves visually matching the pads, verifying their seating with a photo, tightening the caliper bolts by feel, checking for a firm lever, bedding them in with a dozen gentle stops, and signing off.

draft.title: Segway Xyber Front Brake Pad Replacement
disqualifiers: New pads do not visually match the old pads
Brake lever remains spongy after installation
releases: Ready for operation in city traffic and on gravel

steps.title: Verify Replacement Pads
steps.explanation: Ensures the new pads are the correct fit before assembly to prevent brake failure or damage.

fields.prompt: Do the new pads visually match the shape and size of the old pads?
fields.guidance: Place the old and new pads side-by-side. They must have the exact same profile and mounting holes.

steps.title: Install and Verify Pad Seating
steps.explanation: Verifying the pads are seated flat prevents uneven wear or binding during braking.

fields.prompt: Take a photo of the new pads sitting flat and fully seated inside the caliper.
fields.acceptance_description: The new pads sitting perfectly flat and fully seated inside the caliper.
fields.guidance: Ensure the photo clearly shows both pads aligned and fully inserted into the caliper body before reinstalling the wheel.

steps.title: Secure Caliper Bolts
steps.explanation: Securing the caliper bolts prevents the caliper from coming loose under braking, which could put the rider under a car.

fields.prompt: Tighten the caliper mounting bolts firm by feel. Are they securely tightened?
fields.guidance: Tighten the bolts firmly by feel using your hand tools. Ensure there is no play in the caliper.

steps.title: Check Lever Feel
steps.explanation: A spongy lever indicates air in the system or poorly seated pads, making the bike unsafe to ride.

fields.prompt: Squeeze the front brake lever. How does it feel?
fields.guidance: The lever must feel firm and not pull all the way to the grip. If it is spongy, do not ride.

steps.title: Bed In Pads
steps.explanation: Bedding in the pads ensures optimal stopping power before entering traffic.

fields.prompt: Perform a dozen gentle stops down the road to bed in the new pads. Is this complete?
choices: Yes, completed a dozen gentle stops
fields.acceptance_target: Yes, completed a dozen gentle stops
fields.guidance: Ride slowly in a safe area and perform at least 12 gentle, controlled stops to transfer pad material to the rotor.

steps.title: Sign Off
steps.explanation: The mechanic must take responsibility for the safety of the brake system before riding.

fields.prompt: Sign to certify that the front brake pad replacement is complete and the bike is safe to ride.
fields.guidance: Your signature confirms you have completed all checks and believe the bike is safe for traffic.
